To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ORR activity on graphenes can be quantitatively described by the adsorption energy of intermediates; and the ORR performance can be optimized by controlling the adsorption energy.
the ORR activity is determined by the adsorption free energies of intermediates on graphene-based catalysts and can be predicted by DFT calculations.
the ORR activity on graphenes doped by nonmetal elements is determined by the adsorption energy of the ORR intermediates on the surface of the catalysts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new family of electrocatalysts, which can be used for the oxygen reduction reaction (the key process in the energy storage systems) and the water splitting reaction (the key reaction in energy generation systems).
the origin of electrochemical activity of graphene-based catalysts and the design of a metal-free catalyst that exhibits an activity comparable with that of the best known Pt catalysts for the ORR.
the development of new catalysts for the ORR in fuel cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ORR activity is determined by the adsorption strength of the intermediates, which is in agreement with the volcano plot for ORR activity of metal catalysts.
the ORR activity is determined by the free energy of the adsorption of intermediates, which in turn is governed by the electronic properties of the catalyst.
this study provides a clear roadmap towards the development of metal free electrocatalysts that can be competitive to Pt-based catalysts in terms of ORR activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electrocatalytic oxygen reduction activity of graphene-based catalysts is mainly determined by the adsorption free energies of the ORR intermediates, and the best ORR performance is achieved by the materials whose ORR intermediates are most strongly bound to the catalyst surface.
the ORR performance can be improved by tuning the adsorption free energies of intermediates, which are determined by the molecular orbitals of the graphene-based catalyst.
a new class of graphene-based ORR electrocatalysts can be designed and synthesized by doping graphene with nonmetal elements to achieve the best ORR activity, as predicted by the volcano plot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ORR activity can be predicted by the free energy of oxygen adsorption, similarly as for the case of metallic ORR catalysts.
the ORR activity can be enhanced by tuning the adsorption free energies of intermediates on the graphene surface, which is in line with the volcano plot concept.
graphene-based catalysts are a promising alternative to noble metals in electrocatalysis.
